expectation: Membrane ring on activated or tissue-resident lymphocytes (T, NK, some B). In gut mucosa these are common: scattered single cells in the lamina propria and between epithelial cells, and clustered in lymphoid aggregates. Epithelium itself negative.
observed: A: gut villi; a broad yellow streak and some edge glow are artefacts. B, C: crisp ring-shaped cells in the lamina propria and at the epithelial base, epithelium dark. D: a cluster of membrane rings. E: many CD69 ring cells, but CD19 is only haze.
why: Distinct membrane-ring lymphocytes sit in the lamina propria and along the epithelium, with the epithelium unstained, which is the expected pattern for resident CD69+ cells.
notes: Clear ring-shaped CD69+ cells sit in the lamina propria and near the epithelium. The whole-tissue streak and edge glow are artefacts. CD19 shows no cellular structure, so row E cannot confirm co-expression.
